Work, usually with your hands, spoken of as something honourable. You grew up with the slogan 劳动最光荣 and with school chores called 劳动, so it sounds weightier than plain work.
To tell someone what to do from a position above them. You hear rank in it, a boss or an elder giving orders, and saying 您吩咐 to a friend is a playful bow.
A cover story hung up to hide the real purpose. You picture the cloth sign outside an old shop, drawing your eye while the actual business is something else.
Your frame of mind toward how life is treating you. When a friend says 心态好, you know they stay calm through setbacks, and 心态崩了 means they've lost it.
To fob someone off with an excuse so they go away. You can tell it's happening when the answer sounds polite and says nothing at all.
Refined and gentle in a bookish way. You picture glasses, soft speech and good manners, and there's a faint respect in it for people who read.
The working class who own nothing but their labour. You met it as a solemn word in politics class, and now you may joke 我们都是无产阶级 when you can't afford a flat.
To handle something, often just well enough to get by. You can 应付 a hard customer with real skill, but 应付一下 means doing the bare minimum so it goes away.
